review_scope: Bounded static challenge of whether concurrent opens with distinct RequestIds can persist more than one active business day; inspected open handler/domain rule, EF model, migrations/snapshot, provider registration and application-source serialization clues.
disposition: SOURCE_SUPPORTED_CONCURRENT_ACTIVE_DAY_RISK; NO ACTIVE-DAY UNIQUE CONSTRAINT OR HANDLER TRANSACTION FOUND
confidence: High for configured application source and SQL Server EF model/migration scope. Concurrent dual commit is a predicted outcome, not observed SQL execution; external deployment-level coordination remains unknown.

source_evidence.observed: Distinct RequestId replay lookup at 27; reads all currently active day rows at 35-37; applies domain Open at 42-43; creates new row and calls SaveChanges at 51-55 without an enclosing transaction or post-read coordination. Catch only replays same OpenRequestId at 57-61.

Active set is Open, Closing, Reopened (22-24). Open rejects when the supplied snapshot contains any active day (40-43); this is correct for sequential requests but does not serialize independent snapshots.
BusinessDay has primary key and unique OpenRequestId only; no active-state/Status filtered unique index or concurrency token shown.
BusinessDays table is created with Status and OpenRequestId, and the only table index added in this migration is unique IX_BusinessDays_OpenRequestId.
Snapshot shows required Status, PK Id and unique OpenRequestId; no active-day unique index. Migration-source scan found no later migration adding one for BusinessDays.

source_evidence.signature: FalahDbContext provider and business-day open route
source_evidence.observed: Configured provider is SQL Server. Open endpoint at 358-369 invokes handler directly; source path shows no route-level shared transaction/lock.
Nearby comparator explicitly identifies filtered unique Status=Open index as the shift race-safety net; this is for Shifts only and does not protect BusinessDays.

source_evidence.signature: filtered unique open Shift index creation
source_evidence.observed: Migration creates unique IX_Shifts_Status filtered to Status=Open; no BusinessDays equivalent in migration set.

predicted_interleaving: T1 and T2 have distinct RequestIds and both query before either insert; each sees no active BusinessDay.
Each calls BusinessDayRules.Open with an empty active-day list and receives a new Open record.
Each inserts a distinct Id and distinct unique OpenRequestId. Without an active-day constraint or shared lock, both inserts are compatible with visible schema and can commit.
effect: Two rows may remain in an active status (Open/Closing/Reopened), making first-active readers such as BusinessDayGate ambiguous and allowing financial operations to stamp different active day IDs. Exact user-visible or accounting effect depends on query ordering and subsequent operations.
counterevidence: Same OpenRequestId is protected by unique index and replay handling; candidate specifically uses distinct IDs.
BusinessDayRules correctly blocks a second active row in a sequentially refreshed read.
OpenShift demonstrates the application uses a filtered unique index for an analogous single-active invariant, but that index is Shift-only.
SQL Server provider plus RCSI does not itself establish uniqueness; no row/range/application lock was found in the shown open path.
External reverse proxy, scheduler, service host or database trigger coordination was not certified; source scan is not proof about deployment infrastructure.
application_serialization_check: Static scan across src/**/*.cs for OpenBusinessDayHandler references and business-day lock/semaphore/transaction/app-lock patterns found only the handler and ordinary business-day transaction handlers (e.g. close); no open-specific shared semaphore, SQL application lock, transaction-held active-day lock or endpoint wrapper was located. This is bounded source-search evidence, not deployment inspection.
recommendation: Use database-enforced single-active ownership shared by Open and Reopen (for example a carefully designed active-state key/filtered unique constraint or singleton ownership row claimed transactionally), with explicit repair of pre-existing duplicates before migration. Ensure all active-day statuses used by BusinessDayGate are covered. Keep same-request idempotency. Alternative database transaction/locking design needs cross-process semantics and migration/provider proof.
acceptance_tests: SQL Server integration test with barrier after both active-day reads and two distinct RequestIds proves at most one active day commits; loser gets explicit conflict and no second row.
Same RequestId concurrent replay returns one stable day.
Include active-status policy Open/Closing/Reopened and race open versus reopen if they share the invariant.
Run against actual supported SQL Server isolation/provider; assert active reader fails closed if legacy duplicate rows exist.
runtime_limitations: No migration applied, database queried or written, app built/run, or concurrent test executed. Source predicts the race under ordinary parallel requests but no actual double-commit is claimed.
reviewed_scope_only: BusinessDays active-day uniqueness. Do not infer the separate FIN-009 financial finding completion or claim any repair implemented.
